investigation: Amazon AC catalog growth vs. normalization backlog — read-only, no Products 2 write performed
trigger: Mission required verifying current AC quality/coverage status against ADR-305's 2026-09-07 finding ('valid_amazon_offers for air_conditioner is still 0... normalization-drop, NOT fixed this pass').

rpc_result.note: valid_amazon_offers moved from 0 (ADR-305, 2026-09-07) to 1 — negligible improvement in comparison-visible depth despite a much larger raw catalog, per below.

direct_query_result.query: products p join product_stores ps on ps.product_id=p.id where p.category='air_conditioner' and ps.store_id=2 (Amazon)

by_creation_day.note: same day as commit ca3295c7 ('discover-firecrawl never set products.slug, silently blocking every scheduled new-product creation since inception') and ADR-305's own accessory-reclassification fix.

interpretation: The discover-firecrawl slug fix (2026-09-07) unblocked a large backlog of Amazon AC product creation — 255 new Amazon AC storefront products appeared in a single day, then 13 more the next. This is a genuinely large, real catalog now sitting in the storefront layer (products/product_stores). But 268 of the 270 (99.3%) are NOT linked to any canonical_product_id — i.e. never staged into normalized_product_observations / the TPS knowledge layer — so none of this new inventory is visible in cross-store AC comparison. This is the same normalization-staging defect ADR-305 already found and explicitly left open ('a materially larger, cross-category investigation than Amazon AC scope bounds'), now visibly much larger in absolute row count because the upstream discovery blocker that was suppressing it got fixed the same day.
products_2_boundary: This mission's mandate places WRITE/MODIFY/REFACTOR/MIGRATE/REMATCH/MERGE/SPLIT/BACKFILL/REDEFINE of canonical identity, product_matches semantics, and the TPS knowledge layer OFF LIMITS without separate founder approval. Running the normalization pipeline (npm run tps:normalize / scripts/tps-core/normalize-incremental.ts) to link these 268 rows would populate canonical_product_id and touch product_matches-adjacent structures — this IS a Products 2 write by the mission's own definition. NOT executed. Flagged below as PRODUCTS_2_CHANGE_PROPOSED for separate founder approval, per ADR-099's own standing caution that this pipeline must never be run ad hoc/concurrently with the hourly scheduler and must be --dry-run first.

correction_2026_09_08_later_same_day.trigger: Founder question: is the 268 a normal backlog waiting for the usual pipeline, or a real defect blocking linkage? Re-investigated read-only.
correction_2026_09_08_later_same_day.finding: The original 'never staged into normalized_product_observations' claim above was WRONG and is corrected here. Normalization for Amazon (store_id='2') is actively running (8,663 total normalized_product_observations for store_id='2', as recent as 2026-09-08T12:08:49Z). The TPS knowledge layer's own category label for air conditioners is 'ac' (not 'air_conditioner' — a naming mismatch between the storefront layer's products.category and the TPS layer's detected_category, which caused the original mis-diagnosis). Querying the correct label found 244 'ac' rows normalized for store_id='2' in the last 3 days alone (1,243 all-time), and EVERY sampled row already carries a real, populated canonical_product_id.
correction_2026_09_08_later_same_day.proof_of_the_actual_gap: The exact same product exists in both layers with different outcomes. Example: 'Fisher Window Air Conditioner Cold 18000 Btu - FWAC-H18CF' has a normalized_product_observations row with canonical_product_id='980ac6af-aa7b-4988-8c3c-371b8b51943f' (observed_at 2026-09-08T06:09:16Z) — but the corresponding storefront products row (id='ba9ae502-b0d0-4529-af07-870193fdb133', created_at 2026-09-07T16:00:16Z) still shows canonical_product_id=null. Confirmed on 4 separate title matches (Fisher, Nikai, Hisense, Aston), same pattern every time.
correction_2026_09_08_later_same_day.real_root_cause: The gap is NOT in matching/normalization (that already succeeded). It is in the SEPARATE storefront-identity-projection step (products.canonical_product_id) that is supposed to copy a TPS-layer link back onto the storefront products row a customer-facing query actually reads — the likely candidate is scripts/tps-core/project-storefront-identity.ts / npm run tps:storefront-link, though this was not traced line-by-line (would require reading that script's own logic, deliberately not done to stay strictly read-only/observational this pass).
correction_2026_09_08_later_same_day.not_ac_specific: Checked across ALL Amazon categories, same store: tv 1119 linked / 3062 unlinked, air_conditioner 2/268, laptop 33/193, monitor 106/134, audio 46/113, tablet 35/96, smartphone 21/74, camera 16/106, appliance 60/162 — every category shows the identical pattern. This is a systemic storefront-projection lag across the entire Amazon catalog, not an AC-specific or even a normalization-specific defect.
correction_2026_09_08_later_same_day.verdict: REAL_DEFECT, not a normal backlog waiting its turn — the hard part (identity matching) already happened successfully; what's stuck is a downstream propagation/projection step, and it is stuck platform-wide for this merchant, not specifically for AC.
correction_2026_09_08_later_same_day.products_2_boundary_reaffirmed: Still not fixed, still not run — reading project-storefront-identity.ts's logic or running it would be exactly the kind of Products-2-adjacent action this mission is not authorized to perform. This correction only sharpens the diagnosis; it does not change the boundary.
